Bạn là người đã đi đủ xa để nhận ra điều gì là tình yêu thật sự, và điều gì chỉ là tiếng vọng của ký ức. • Vũ Trụ không bao giờ đưa ai trở lại cuộc đời bạn một cách ngẫu nhiên. desc: Đã bao giờ bạn ngước nhìn cái bóng nhỏ thó của mình dính chặt dưới gót chân trong một buổi trưa tròn bóng, rồi vô thức nghĩ về một người xa lạ ở bên kia hành tinh, kẻ cũng đang ngước mắt nhìn trời lúc 12 giờ trưa, nhưng cái bóng dưới chân lại đổ dài về phía hoàn toàn trái ngược? Họ tựa như hai mảnh ghép soi qua chiếc gương Trái Đất. Dù sống chung một nhịp đếm thời gian, cùng vội vã thức giấc hay nhấp ngụm cà phê lúc 7 giờ sáng, họ lại chịu sự chi phối của hai mùa hoàn toàn đối lập. Khi bạn đang quay cuồng dưới cái nắng hè rực rỡ, thì họ lại trùm chăn co ro giữa cái lạnh âm độ của mùa đông. Trong đời sống hằng ngày, ta bỗng nhận ra Antiscians chẳng ở đâu xa xôi, mà hiện diện ngay trong những mối quan hệ thân thuộc nhất: người bạn tri kỷ, đồng nghiệp chung bàn, hay chính người thương bên cạnh. Họ cùng bước đi bên bạn trên một chặng đường, cùng đối mặt với một biến cố (như một quầng mặt trời rọi xuống), nhưng cách cái bóng nội tâm của mỗi người ngả xuống lại trắc trở vô cùng. Người chọn xông pha đối diện, kẻ chọn thu mình phòng thủ; người muốn trút hết tâm tư, kẻ lại lặng lẽ giấu kín vào trong. Nhưng khái niệm về những "kẻ bóng ngược" lại mỉm cười xoa dịu ta: việc hai cái bóng ngả về hai hướng đối lập chẳng phân định đúng sai, mà chỉ vì cả hai đang đứng ở hai bán cầu của trải nghiệm. desc: David Walliams' career and controversies including Britain's Got Talent and Little Britain David Walliams has been accused of grooming young fans and harassing women in the workplace, after failing to stop the Guardian and ITN publishing claims against him. A three-year investigation, external by the two news organisations alleged the Little Britain star and former Britain's Got Talent judge preyed on teenage girls as young as 15 and young women, external for s3xual purposes. He had sought a High Court injunction to prevent publication, with his lawyers arguing if allegations were made public Walliams would likely k!ll himself. The court refused the request. Walliams has denied all of the allegations but in a letter to journalists working on the investigation acknowledged "at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with". He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me." The 55-year-old became a household name in the early 2000s through Little Britain, his comedy sketch show with Matt Lucas broadcast on the BBC. Walliams published his first children's book, The Boy in the Dress, in 2008, and his stories soon became best-sellers and led to comparisons with Roald Dahl. His 23 children's books have sold more than 50 million copies worldwide, but he was dropped by publisher HarperCollins in 2025 after allegations of inappropriate behaviour, which he denied. In 2012, Walliams became a judge on Britain's Got Talent, and was voted best TV judge at the National TV Awards (NTAs) four times. He was replaced as a judge in 2022. Before entering showbusiness, Walliams was born David Williams but changed his surname's spelling to avoid having the same name as another member of entertainment union Equity. He was married to Dutch model Lara Stone from 2010 to 2015 and they have a son. That hasn't stopped speculation about Walliams' sexuality. He has described himself as "bi-curious" and called his 2012 autobiography Camp David – but said he isn't attracted to men in the way he is to women. Walliams and Lucas won a string of awards for Little Britain including three Baftas and two International Emmys, and the programme was watched by 10 million people in the UK. But in the two decades since it ended, views about the show and what is and is not acceptable to joke about have radically altered. The programme has been criticised for its use of blackface and for stereotyping and mocking characters from minority and marginalised groups. In the wake of the Black Lives Matter movement in 2020, Little Britain was removed from streaming services including BBC iPlayer, Netflix and BritBox. Another of the duo's shows, 2010 airport comedy Come Fly With Me, was also removed from BritBox a decade after its original broadcast, due to the show's use of racial stereotypes and using make-up to portray people from other ethnic groups. Little Britain was restored to iPlayer in 2022 with several scenes cut out. Walliams and Lucas said they had re-edited the show to "better reflect the changes in the cultural landscape since the show was made". Not all the criticisms of Walliams have involved new standards being applied to older work. Walliams had to apologise after two charity performances, during which he yanked down not only the trousers but also the underwear of actor Jeremy Edwards and music producer Mark Ronson. In 2020, he was booed while hosting the NTAs after making a joke about Caroline Flack being out of work, at a time when she had stepped down from hosting Love Island and was waiting to appear in court, having been charged for actual bodily harm following a row with her boyfriend. Later in 2022, he was replaced as a judge on Britain's Got Talent after a Guardian story about a leaked recording of Walliams making insulting remarks about contestants during breaks from filming.

desc: The Salinas City Elementary School District is preparing to delete its Facebook and Instagram accounts on Nov. 20, citing concerns about student privacy and the potential misuse of student photos by artificial intelligence tools. The district raised concerns about Meta’s proposed changes to its terms of service, which it believes could pose risks to student privacy. "We would have to indemnify Meta against any problems caused by its AI. In other words, if a bad actor took Meta's AI tool, used our student photos in a really disturbing way, it would be on us. It wouldn't be on Meta," said Mary Duan, Director of Communications and Community Outreach for Salinas City Elementary School District. On Nov. 5, Meta announced that the proposed changes to its terms of service were on hold and would not take effect on Nov. 20. Meta’s vice president of strategic response communication shared a statement on X, saying, "We’ve heard publishers’ feedback on our proposed ads and business terms update. We care deeply about our partners and do not plan to make policy changes without a full consultation with industry groups and leaders." Despite Meta’s decision to pause the changes, Salinas City Elementary School District is not altering its plans. Other local school districts are also monitoring Meta’s plans. The Santa Rita Union School District said in a statement, "As the situation continues to evolve, we will carefully evaluate any changes that may affect our practices and take appropriate steps to safeguard student information." Meanwhile, the Salinas Union High School District stated that its accounts will remain active, saying, "SUHSD has been closely monitoring these developments and will continue assessing how they apply to student privacy and district operation." Once the Salinas City Elementary School District’s social media accounts are deleted, families will still be able to access school photos and updates through the district’s website and ParentSquare, a secure portal.
